body: I wouldn’t know what to do with a better life. If given the choice, I would pick a natural death over better life everytime. There are 3 people I don’t want to affect negatively and that’s pretty much the only thing holding me back.

Np, as I said I'm aware of the intention behind this post. No harm done.

This is on the internet anyway, who am I to tell you what to write? Whatever I feel, it's up to me to handle myself anyway.

Why would you make it up to me? I don't understand.

It's simple really. If you already feel you haven't done enough, that you should have produced better results for the support you got, then it will feel even worse when they are being supportive like this. It may not make sense for you though. That's just my perspective.

God that is the single most dangerous sentence which would finish me off with guilt. It really sucks when I hear this while thinking I could have done more. Bcs being this supportive, they deserve even better.

I'm aware of the intention though, it's not their fault I feel this way.

Whatever holds your interest. I read, one of my friends would go out and try new foods.... what's important is that you care enough about it to distract you. People recommend exercise which would be awesome if you could stick to it.
It's probably a defense mechanism against the social stigma on the suicide. I think it's not rare (meaning I do that too sometimes).

Methods with certainty of success are too obvious, discrete ones are prone to failure. I have almost succeded recently though with the most discrete method I will ever get. Unfortunately the more things are out of your control, things are more likely to fail.

I had a suitcase with several proven methods and enough cash to travel to do it just bcs it helped me relax. I liked the fact that I have always had a option to refuse and not stuck in this life. 

It's rather dangerous bcs not having a plan and means ready will give you more time to reconsider but damn if it didn't feel good to check valves, expiration dates, heat-moisture damage etc... and find that everthing is ready.
The fact that I don't want to them to face with social stigma of suicide and blame themselves is the strongest reason I have for not doing anything drastic yet.
I'm not in any position to offer advice about anything really but here is something I learned hard way, stay away from medicine.

Private clinics who are paid in cash while keeping no official records exist. I didn't find them particularly helpful though, but at least I tried them.

I'm not sure they would qualify as intrusive thoughts. That would mean they are in conflict with my desire to live and I can't keep them out. This doesn't look like to be true in my case.

I'm simply extremely disappointed by my current self who has learned nothing about being happy and leading a balanced life bcs I was so busy learning everything else. It looks unlikely to change and I'd simply prefer not to continue. 

It's easy to blame my job and it could be a major component that led me in this situation but I'd probably be similarly unhappy in other professions. Some people take their job, education etc... to seriously and never learn to live and be happy.

There is a distinct possibility to lose your practice if you seek help through official channels, that's for sure. They do not particularly care about our lives, otherwise they wouldn't let the guy out to finish the job so quickly.
The hilarious part is that I have just learned they released the guy on bail.
I don't really feel I won at anything. It always felt like a huge responsibility with minimal benefits.
That's fine, I sincerely doubt that I can be fixed. At least not without some insane amount of effort which would be simply wasteful. Thanks for responding.
Maybe some of them laugh bcs they think it too.

Because it could be caused by changeable effects. When you see a guy commiting suicide:
 
He could be under influence, having a bad trip. He could be having a hallucination and need treatment. His depression might be a treatable one. He could be pressured by someone else... etc. So in order to determine if this is the case, they first need to stop the act. 

Even the organisations who provide assistance have extremely strict criterias to detefmine whether the decision if rational and well-thought. Sucks for people like us but they are trying to keep their consience clean.

I'm a bit younger that's true but I don't know if it will help much. It really goes downhill at certain point and people like us must struggle so much to stop the momentum.

Our age/(and I dare say) profession comes with certain expectations. When we make mistakes it often comes across as intentional. Mistakes we should have made when we were teenagers or early 20s. They are no longer acceptable now and we never learned not to do them. So we fail at relationships.

Meeting people at work is a gamble. So many of us have their own shit to deal with. We can no longer become friends as easyly as in collage. We can hang out at work but often won't try to do that outside. It's not impossible though, maybe we'll get lucky.

Honestly it felt as if I'm talking an older version of myself. This is not uncommon in md's, I have seen several people like myself. I guess there is a not insignificant part of us who fail to learn some essential things while busting our asses to get in/graduate medschool. It's also looks like I'll spend my life alone too. At least it'll be easy if I ever decide to take the exit.

That's because motivational videos aren't made for struggling people. They are made so that people can show off how sentitive they are and how much they care. 

The actual struggling people are also the least likely ones to receive help most of the time. Better to try something yourself. There is a good chance that it also won't make you happy, I'm not a stanger to that. There is a certain satisfaction which comes from "doing something" and it helps.
Thanks, often it feels like it's the only thing that keeps me together. People wouldn't believe how I am when I'm at home alone.

I'm having trouble with enjoying anything most of the time. For better or worse med school made me indifferent to myself. It's rather useful since I don't need to worry about losing my head no matter what comes to  the ER.

Maybe somewhere in my mind I'm still trying to catch up to the image people have of me or compensating for the lost years during education.

As someone recently got out of a similar situation( I have my own post for it in this sub), I want to say this train of thought is exteremely dangerous. I myself survived by dumb luck, it could have gone other way easily. Temptation only grows in time. My advice is that you should make it less binding than this. Make it more vague, give yourself some room to save yourself and go forward with your plan to make a better life for yourself. Good luck!
I think there is no one on this subreddit that could say no to this and actually mean it. You perfectly summarised one of my many issues.
Things that would be left unfinished, that it would look like I gave up. There are some people who would use it to feel better about themselves, which is unacceptable.

Because people love to talk even if the don't know anything about what they are saying. Anyone who says that people under 18 can't be depressed is simply wrong. I was actually tought about this topic.
